headline: Earnings jump as Macau offsets Vegas and Boston softness
summary_short: Wynn Resorts' Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.9% y/y to $1,856.9M as Macau growth and a modest Las Vegas gain outweighed a decline at Encore Boston Harbor; net income more than doubled to $140.1M and diluted EPS rose to $1.32 from $0.64.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.9% y/y to $1,856.9M, led by Wynn Palace (+$113.8M) and Wynn Macau (+$7.3M), with Las Vegas up modestly (+$4.6M) and Encore Boston Harbor down $6.4M. Adjusted Property EBITDAR rose to $568.3M from $552.4M as Wynn Palace's $44.3M gain outweighed declines at Las Vegas (-$19.6M), Encore Boston Harbor (-$7.8M) and Wynn Macau (-$1.0M). Net income more than doubled to $140.1M ($1.32 diluted EPS) from $66.2M ($0.64), aided by a $43.3M favorable derivatives-fair-value swing versus a $1.1M loss. The board declared a $0.25/share dividend and the company repurchased $75.0M of stock. Cash was $1,573.4M; total debt was $10,724.7M plus $1,429.0M current. No formal guidance was issued; Wynn Al Marjan Island remains on track to open September 2027.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by Wynn Palace (+$113.8M) and Wynn Macau (+$7.3M) plus modest Las Vegas growth (+$4.6M), partly offset by a $6.4M decline at Encore Boston Harbor.

Adjusted Property EBITDAR rose as Wynn Palace's $44.3M gain (mass-market table win 29.7% vs 22.3% a year ago) outweighed declines at Las Vegas (-$19.6M), Encore Boston Harbor (-$7.8M) and Wynn Macau (-$1.0M).
Margin expansion is arithmetic: operating income grew 12.5% while revenue grew only 6.9%, lifting margin 0.8ppt.

Growth was aided by a $43.3M favorable swing in the change in derivatives fair value (a $43.3M gain vs a $1.1M loss a year ago) and lower foreign-currency remeasurement losses ($2.7M vs $36.2M), per the income statement.
Net margin rose 3.7ppt because net income more than doubled (+111.5%) while revenue grew only 6.9% — profit growth arithmetically outpacing revenue growth.
Basic EPS grew 114.1% versus net income's 111.5% gain because basic weighted-average shares fell about 0.9% y/y (103.5M to 102.6M) on continued buybacks.
Diluted EPS grew 106.3% versus net income's 111.5% gain because diluted weighted-average shares fell about 0.8% y/y (103.8M to 103.0M) on continued buybacks.

CEO Craig Billings cited a monthly Adjusted Property EBITDAR record in Las Vegas in May and strong Macau performance, while noting rapid progress on Wynn Al Marjan Island, on track to open September 2027.
